messages.subject: Latent Interactions and "covariance matrix of latent variables is not positive definite"
parts:
Hello and greetings!

I am trying to run a model with latent interactions in it. The focal predictors are longitudinal in nature and measured in two occasions. I have tried to apply the indProd function from semTools package in order to produce the product indicators for the interaction factor. The moderators (CONFCOMP_T1 and CONFREP_T1 ) are one-item factors. The model below is based on the metric invariance test that showed an acceptable fit. A point could be of relevance, there are dropouts in the longitudinal measures and I tried to use missing="FIML" in the fit function to account for that.

Int.dat1 <- indProd(notypos,  var1 = c("RAC1_T1", "RAC2_T1", "RAC3_T1", "RAC4_T1", "RAC5_T1"),
                              var2 = c("CONF1_T1"),
                              match = FALSE, doubleMC = TRUE)

Int.dat2 <- indProd(Int.dat1, var1 = c("RAC1_T1", "RAC2_T1", "RAC3_T1", "RAC4_T1", "RAC5_T1"),
                              var2 = c("CONF2_T1"),
                              match = FALSE, doubleMC = TRUE)

Int.dat3 <- indProd(Int.dat2, var1 = c("RNC1_T1", "RNC2_T1", "RNC3_T1", "RNC4_T1"),
                              var2 = c("CONF1_T1"),
                              match = FALSE, doubleMC = TRUE)

Int.dat4 <- indProd(Int.dat3, var1 = c("RNC1_T1", "RNC2_T1", "RNC3_T1", "RNC4_T1"),
                              var2 = c("CONF2_T1"),
                              match = FALSE, doubleMC = TRUE)


model.int <- '
            RAC_T1 =~ RAC1_T1 + RAC2_T1 + RAC3_T1 + RAC4_T1 + RAC5_T1
            RNC_T1 =~ RNC1_T1 + RNC2_T1 + RNC3_T1 + RNC4_T1
            CONFCOMP_T1 =~ CONF1_T1 ##competition
            CONFREP_T1 =~ CONF2_T1  ##bad reputation
            AC_T1 =~ ac1f*AC1_T1 + ac2f*AC2_T1 + ac3f*AC3_T1 + ac4f*AC4_T1 + ac5f*AC5_T1
            AC_T2 =~ ac1f*AC1_T2 + ac2f*AC2_T2 + ac3f*AC3_T2 + ac4f*AC4_T2 + ac5f*AC5_T2
            NC_T1 =~ nc1f*NC1_T1 + nc2f*NC2_T1 + nc3f*NC3_T1 + nc4f*NC4_T1 + nc5f*NC5_T1
            NC_T2 =~ nc1f*NC1_T2 + nc2f*NC2_T2 + nc3f*NC3_T2 + nc4f*NC4_T2 + nc5f*NC5_T2

            int.RAC_CONF1 =~ RAC1_T1.CONF1_T1 + RAC2_T1.CONF1_T1 + RAC3_T1.CONF1_T1 + RAC4_T1.CONF1_T1 + RAC5_T1.CONF1_T1
            int.RAC_CONF2 =~ RAC1_T1.CONF2_T1 + RAC2_T1.CONF2_T1 + RAC3_T1.CONF2_T1 + RAC4_T1.CONF2_T1 + RAC5_T1.CONF2_T1
           
            int.RNC_CONF1 =~ RNC1_T1.CONF1_T1 + RNC2_T1.CONF1_T1 + RNC3_T1.CONF1_T1 + RNC4_T1.CONF1_T1
            int.RNC_CONF2 =~ RNC1_T1.CONF2_T1 + RNC2_T1.CONF2_T1 + RNC3_T1.CONF2_T1 + RNC4_T1.CONF2_T1
           
           
            ##covarainces between interaction and first-order factors are freely estimated:
           
            int.RAC_CONF1 ~~ RAC_T1
            int.RAC_CONF1 ~~ CONFCOMP_T1
           
            int.RAC_CONF2 ~~ RAC_T1
            int.RAC_CONF2 ~~ CONFREP_T1
           
           
            int.RNC_CONF1 ~~ RNC_T1
            int.RNC_CONF1 ~~ CONFCOMP_T1
           
            int.RNC_CONF2 ~~ RNC_T1
            int.RNC_CONF2 ~~ CONFREP_T1
           
     
            ##correlated residuals between T1 and T2 Items
           
            AC1_T1 ~~ AC1_T2

#### Residual covariances between the same indicator are freely estimated


##int.RAC_CONF1
RAC1_T1.CONF1_T1 ~~ t1*RAC2_T1.CONF1_T1 + t1*RAC3_T1.CONF1_T1 + t1*RAC4_T1.CONF1_T1 + t1*RAC5_T1.CONF1_T1
RAC2_T1.CONF1_T1 ~~ t1*RAC3_T1.CONF1_T1 + t1*RAC4_T1.CONF1_T1 + t1*RAC5_T1.CONF1_T1
RAC3_T1.CONF1_T1 ~~ t1*RAC4_T1.CONF1_T1 + t1*RAC5_T1.CONF1_T1
RAC4_T1.CONF1_T1 ~~ t1*RAC5_T1.CONF1_T1


##int.RAC_CONF2
RAC1_T1.CONF2_T1 ~~ t2*RAC2_T1.CONF2_T1 + t2*RAC3_T1.CONF2_T1 + t2*RAC4_T1.CONF2_T1 + t2*RAC5_T1.CONF2_T1
RAC2_T1.CONF2_T1 ~~ t2*RAC3_T1.CONF2_T1 + t2*RAC4_T1.CONF2_T1 + t2*RAC5_T1.CONF2_T1
RAC3_T1.CONF2_T1 ~~ t2*RAC4_T1.CONF2_T1 + t2*RAC5_T1.CONF2_T1
RAC4_T1.CONF2_T1 ~~ t2*RAC5_T1.CONF2_T1


##int.RNC_CONF1
RNC1_T1.CONF1_T1 ~~ t3*RNC2_T1.CONF1_T1 + t3*RNC3_T1.CONF1_T1 + t3*RNC4_T1.CONF1_T1
RNC2_T1.CONF1_T1 ~~ t3*RNC3_T1.CONF1_T1 + t3*RNC4_T1.CONF1_T1
RNC3_T1.CONF1_T1 ~~ t3*RNC4_T1.CONF1_T1


##int.RNC_CONF2
RNC1_T1.CONF2_T1 ~~ t4*RNC2_T1.CONF2_T1 + t4*RNC3_T1.CONF2_T1 + t4*RNC4_T1.CONF2_T1
RNC2_T1.CONF2_T1 ~~ t4*RNC3_T1.CONF2_T1 + t4*RNC4_T1.CONF2_T1
RNC3_T1.CONF2_T1 ~~ t4*RNC4_T1.CONF2_T1


'

fit.model.int <- sem(model.int, data = Int.dat4, meanstructure = TRUE, estimator = "MLR", std.lv= TRUE, missing="FIML")


When I am running this structural model, it is showing the below error:

Warning messages:
1: In lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, cluster = cluster,  :
  lavaan WARNING: 107 cases were deleted due to missing values in
          exogenous variable(s), while fixed.x = TRUE.
2: In lav_object_post_check(object) :
  lavaan WARNING: covariance matrix of latent variables
                is not positive definite;
                use lavInspect(fit, "cov.lv") to investigate.

I am quite new in SEM and it would be a great help if you could kindly mention the possible causes of these errors. Any advice in this regard will be much appreciated.

Thanks and have a nice day!

Best regards,
Oliur

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Latent Interactions and "covariance matrix of latent variables is not positive definite"
parts: They are warnings, not error messages.

> Warning messages:
> 1: In lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, cluster = cluster,  :
>   lavaan WARNING: 107 cases were deleted due to missing values in
>           exogenous variable(s), while fixed.x = TRUE.

This one is harmless, and just points out that have 'lost' 107 cases,
because they had missing values on exogenous 'x' covariates (and lavaan
uses fixed.x = TRUE per default).

> 2: In lav_object_post_check(object) :
>   lavaan WARNING: covariance matrix of latent variables
>                 is not positive definite;
>                 use lavInspect(fit, "cov.lv") to investigate.

This is a potential sign of model misfit, but it could also be due to a
relatively small sample size. To see the latent covariance matrix in
correlation matrix, you can use lavInspect(fit, "cor.lv")

Yves.

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: Latent Interactions and "covariance matrix of latent variables is not positive definite"
parts:
In this case, I think the warning might be a sign of model misspecification. When one of the variables used for the interaction term has a single indicator you don't want to include residual covariances for the interaction latent variable since this ends up being redundant with the latent interaction variables (here you're trying to estimate the latent variable and all residual covariances among the indicators for each latent interaction variable). I'd remove all the residual covariances at the end.

Alex
